'''Douglas Joel Futuyma''' (born 24 April 1942) is an American [[evolutionary biologist]]. He is a Distinguished Professor in the Department of Ecology and Evolution at [[Stony Brook University]] in [[Stony Brook, New York]] and a Research Associate on staff at the [[American Museum of Natural History]] in [[New York City]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web|last1=Futuyma|first1=Douglas J.|title=Curriculum Vitae|url=http://life.bio.sunysb.edu/ee/cv_pdf/FutuymaCV2013.pdf|website=Stony Brook University|access-date=8 June 2015|date=October 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106141645/http://life.bio.sunysb.edu/ee/cv_pdf/FutuymaCV2013.pdf|archive-date=2014-01-06}}</ref> His research focuses on [[speciation]] and [[population biology]].<ref name=dept>{{cite web|title=Ecology & Evolution Department Faculty|url=http://life.bio.sunysb.edu/ee/faculty.html|website=Stony Brook University|access-date=8 June 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150612121208/http://life.bio.sunysb.edu/ee/faculty.html|archive-date=12 June 2015}}</ref> Futuyma is the author of a widely used [[undergraduate]] textbook on [[evolution]] and is also known for his work in public outreach,<ref name=leidy>{{cite web|title=Joseph Leidy Award for Stony Brook Biologist|date=September 13, 2012|url=http://www.ansp.org/about/press-room/releases/2012/leidy-award/|publisher=The Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University |access-date=15 April 2015}}</ref> particularly in advocating against [[creationism]].<ref name=ncse>{{cite web|title=Congratulations to Douglas J. Futuyma|url=http://ncse.com/news/2012/09/congratulations-to-douglas-j-futuyma-0014577|website=National Center for Science Education|access-date=8 June 2015|date=13 September 2012}}</ref>

==Education==
Futuyma graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] from [[Cornell University]]. He received his [[Master's degree|M.S.]] in 1966 and his [[Doctorate|Ph.D.]] in [[zoology]] in 1969, both from the [[University of Michigan, Ann Arbor]].<ref name=cv />

==Academic career==
Futuyma began his career in the Department of Ecology and Evolution at [[Stony Brook University]] in 1969 and was appointed Distinguished Professor in 2001. He served as the chair of the Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at [[University of Michigan, Ann Arbor]] from 2002-2003 and as the Lawrence B. Slobodkin Collegiate Professor in that department from 2003-2004 before returning to Stony Brook in 2004.<ref name=cv />

Futuyma served as the president of the [[Society for the Study of Evolution]] in 1987, of the [[American Society of Naturalists]] in 1994, and of the [[American Institute of Biological Sciences]] in 2008. He has served as the editor of the [[scientific journal]]s ''[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]]'' and the ''[[Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics]]'' (2002-2026).<ref name=cv /><ref name="AREES">{{cite journal |last1=Futuyma |first1=Douglas J. |title=AREES at 50: A Semicentennial Celebration |journal=Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics |date=2 November 2019 |volume=50 |issue=1 |pages=1–26 |doi=10.1146/annurev-ecolsys-110218-024647 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Annual Review of Ecology, Evolution, and Systematics, Planning Editorial Committee - Volume 57, 2026 |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/db/directory?2026,ecolsys |website=Annual Reviews Directory |access-date=18 August 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==Research==
Futuyma's research examines [[speciation]] and [[population biology]], particularly the evolutionary interactions between [[herbivorous]] insects and their plant [[host (biology)|hosts]] and the implications for evolution of [[host specificity]].<ref name=dept />

==Teaching and outreach==
Futuyma is well known for his success in teaching and public outreach.<ref name=leidy /> He is the author of several textbooks, most notably the very widely used authoritative text ''Evolutionary Biology'' (in its third edition, published 1998)<ref>{{cite journal | last=Fairbairn | first=Daphne J. | title=Evolutionary Biology Third Edition by Douglas J. Futuyma | type=Book review | journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology | volume=73 | issue=4 | date=1998 | issn=0033-5770 | doi=10.1086/420454 | jstor=3037513 | id={{ResearchGatePub|240246490}} | url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Daphne-Fairbairn/publication/240246490_Evolutionary_Biology_Douglas_J_Futuyma/links/576092e708ae2b8d20eb6549/Evolutionary-Biology-Douglas-J-Futuyma.pdf | pages=503–504 | quote-page=504 |quote=the third edition of ''Evolutionary Biology'', like its predecessors, virtually defines the field of evolutionary biology, and will no doubt find a place on the bookshelves of almost all practicing evolutionary biologists.}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Futuyma |first=Douglas J. |title=Evolutionary Biology |year=1998 |edition=3rd |location=Sunderland, MA |publisher=[[Sinauer Associates]] |isbn=978-0-87893-189-7}}</ref> and a simplified version targeted explicitly to undergraduates, ''Evolution'' (in its fourth edition, published 2017).<ref name=":0">{{cite book|title=Evolution|last=Futuyma|first=Douglas J.|publisher=Sinauer Associates|year=2017|isbn=978-1605356051|edition=4th|location=Sunderland, MA}}</ref> The latter text has been positively reviewed as important to the successful teaching of evolution, though less comprehensive than the former.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Applequist|first1=Wendy L.|title=''Evolution'' by D. J. Futuyma|journal=Systematic Botany|date=1 April 2006|volume=31|issue=2|pages=441|doi=10.1600/036364406777585711|s2cid=86238537}}</ref> He has also co-edited a more advanced book composed of edited reviews, ''Coevolution'',<ref>{{cite book|editor1-last=Futuyma|editor1-first=Douglas J.|editor2-last=Slatkin|editor2-first=Montgomery|title=Coevolution|date=1983|publisher=Sinauer Assoc.|location=Sunderland, Mass.|isbn=9780878932283|edition=[2nd printing].}}</ref> with [[Montgomery Slatkin]]; it received mixed reviews from those in the field.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kitchell|first1=Jennifer A.|title=Reviewed Work: Coevolution. by Douglas J. Futuyma, Montgomery Slatkin|journal=Paleobiology|date=1983|volume=9|issue=3|pages=308–313|jstor=2400662|doi=10.1017/S0094837300007715|s2cid=89592140 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Jollie|first1=Malcolm|title=Reviewed Work: Coevolution by Douglas J. Futuyma, Montgomery Slatkin|journal=The Auk|date=April 1984|volume=101|issue=2|pages=410–12|jstor=4086388}}</ref>

Futuyma has also written for a [[popular science|popular audience]] in his book ''Science on Trial: The Case for Evolution'', originally published in 1982, in which he discusses the [[creation–evolution controversy]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Futuyma|first1=Douglas J.|title=Science on trial|date=1983|publisher=Pantheon Books|location=New York|isbn=978-0394706795|edition=1.|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/scienceontrialca0000futu}}</ref> The book has been regarded as highly effective in making the argument for evolution and as a tool for discussing the topic with those who are uncertain; philosopher of biology [[Michael Ruse]] described it as "a first-class book".<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ruse|first1=Michael|title=Reviewed Work: Science on Trial: The Case for Evolution. by Douglas J. Futuyma|journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology|date=September 1983|volume=58|issue=3|pages=395–398|jstor=2828648|doi=10.1086/413388}}</ref> It was also reviewed as suitable for use in undergraduate education.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Weaver|first1=David S.|title=Science on trial. By D.J. Futuyma. New York: Pantheon Books. 1983. xii + 251 pp., figures, tables, appendix, notes, index. $6.95 (paper)|journal=American Journal of Physical Anthropology|date=August 1985|volume=67|issue=4|pages=419–420|doi=10.1002/ajpa.1330670414}}</ref> [[Richard Lewontin]] found the book "lucid" but criticized its presentation, along with other books on the topic published around the same time, as failing to capture the origins of the debate as a social phenomenon.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Lewontin|first1=Richard C.|title=Darwin's Revolution|url=http://www.nybooks.com/articles/archives/1983/jun/16/darwins-revolution/|access-date=8 June 2015|work=The New York Review of Books|date=16 June 1983}}</ref>

Since 2013, Futuyma has been listed on the Advisory Council of the [[National Center for Science Education]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ncse.com/about/advisory-council |title=Advisory Council |website=ncse.com |publisher=[[National Center for Science Education]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130810112828/https://ncse.com/about/advisory-council |archive-date=2013-08-10 |access-date=2018-10-30}}</ref>

Futuyma is [[openly gay]]. He has said that he was initially surprised at the lack of negative career consequences, and that [[LGBT]] visibility is important to progress on [[gay rights]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Silberman|first1=Steve|last2=Koerth-Baker|first2=Maggie|title=Coming Out in the Sciences: Part II—Your stories, today|url=http://boingboing.net/2010/10/11/coming-out-in-the-sc-1.html|website=BoingBoing|access-date=8 June 2015|date=2010-10-11}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Spector|first1=Barbara|title=Gay And Lesbian Scientists Seek Workplace Equality|url=http://www.the-scientist.com/?articles.view/articleNo/12193/title/Gay-And-Lesbian-Scientists-Seek-Workplace-Equality/|website=The Scientist Magazine|access-date=8 June 2015|date=2 March 1992}}</ref> In 1984 he co-authored a [[scientific paper]] critical of the evidence available at the time that [[homosexuality]] might be genetic.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Futuyma|first1=DJ|last2=Risch|first2=SJ|title=Sexual orientation, sociobiology, and evolution.|journal=Journal of Homosexuality|date=1984|volume=9|issue=2–3|pages=157–68|pmid=6687153|doi=10.1300/j082v09n02_10}}</ref> In later editions of his textbook ''Evolution'', Futuyma noted that subsequent research has provided stronger evidence for genetic contributions to sexual orientation, reflecting developments in the field since the publication of the earlier paper.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book |last=Futuyma |first=Douglas J. |title=Evolution |last2=Kirkpatrick |first2=Mark |date=2023 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-767929-6 |edition=5th |location=New York, NY}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Futuyma was named a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1985 and of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1996. He was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 2006.<ref name=cv />

Futuyma was selected as a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] in 1992 and as a [[Fulbright Fellow]] senior scholar in 1999, awarded for travel to the [[University of Melbourne]] in Australia.<ref name=cv />

He received the Sewall Wright Award from the American Society of Naturalists in 1997<ref name=cv /> and the [[Leidy Award]] from the Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University in 2012.<ref name=leidy />
